contract: Bounded immutable JSON publication at a fixed HTTP origin through EffectIntent and Jobs; no provider replay/no-effect grounds, explicit read-only recovery and job-control-only cancellation.
limits: Host owns stable origin/identity, truthful preflight, authenticated receipts, bounded task pools, clock, Store durability, recovery grants and continuing expiry after job termination.
Finite grace/poll ratio does not bound concurrent wakes or pre-deadline polling; capacity saturation fails closed.
Loopback protocol evidence, not a live vendor integration; no HTTP physical rollback, hot configuration or business drain.

ELZ-052 evolution note: observation added through runtime/telemetry ([:elzoo, :job | :effect, :start | :stop | :exception] events); inputs, outputs, state, delivery and failure guarantees are unchanged; no Contract change, so the Piece ID is kept. The added Need is the telemetry library (1.4.2), already in the dependency closure.

Telemetry handlers run synchronously in the emitting process: a handler's run time is elapsed time; a handler slower than the remaining deadline makes the operation expire exactly as any other delay would. Handlers must be fast and non-blocking (offload work); effect events delay a result's arrival at the owner. Events are observations, not audit; an event may be missing.

grounding.claim: Pinned Cure compilation checks consumed pure declaration/decision types; owned-source audit and finite scenarios do not prove arbitrary consumer or external behavior.
Named executable boundary, ABI, malformed-input and failure scenarios; finite evidence, not quantified proof.

ELZ-052 listed scenarios on PostgreSQL, Oban 2.24.2 and loopback Req: the runner emits [:elzoo, :job, ...] and send/poll emit [:elzoo, :effect, ...] with exactly the documented keys and integer units (payload_bytes a byte count); effect stop outcomes are the translated tags for 404, 503, redirect, duplicate, invalid, pending, dropped, drip and preflight responses and poll maps to unavailable; owner-unavailable and invalid wakes; tenant and queue outside the telemetry grammar are omitted; no payload, credential, origin URL or receipt field in any event; raising, throwing and exiting handlers are detached and change no result, phase or wire count; a 200 ms handler on every event changes no result (added time reported); a runner fault emits [:elzoo, :job, :exception] (reason :raise) and an Adapter fault in send or poll emits [:elzoo, :effect, :exception] (reason :throw or :exit) with an integer duration while the public result or throw/exit is unchanged; deadline-crossing handlers at the runner start (before the owner's expiry reading) and at each effect emission point (send and poll, :start and :stop, before the result's arrival at the owner) yield exactly the outcome of a no-handler run with the injected clock advanced by the same amount, and non-crossing ones the unchanged outcome. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

telemetry.contract: Bounded job-caller observer emits fixed event/outcome/elapsed time; no sensitive values or durable audit promise. ELZ-052: runtime/telemetry :job events (operation :perform) around each runner wake and :effect events (operation :send or :poll) around each send/poll, outside every call_ms, observer_ms and total_ms timer; allowlisted metadata only (adapter, operation, request_ref = derived key, attempt, tenant and queue when they match the telemetry grammar, outcome, reason); handlers synchronous, may be absent, a failing handler is detached by telemetry and changes no result.

config.contract: Checked construction-time binding/origin/queue/limits/callbacks; no hot update.

control.contract: Best-effort Oban cancellation count plus unknown external outcome; host-owned queue/owner recovery, no rollback or business drain.
